title: US Updates H-1B Debarred Employer List: Four Companies Now Barred From Sponsoring Workers
excerpt: The Department of Labor's latest update adds Sherwood Academy to the disqualified list and maintains bans on GowraTech, Renotek Group, and Seeloz through 2028.
body:
• The US Department of Labor updated its H-1B debarred employer list effective July 1, 2026, with four companies currently barred from sponsoring H-1B workers.
  • The newest addition is Sherwood at Mount Dora, Inc. (dba Sherwood Academy), debarred from May 2026 through May 2028 for willful violations.
  • A separate willful violator list names 13 employers including staffing firms and tech companies found to have committed serious H-1B program violations.
  • Indian professionals, who receive the majority of H-1B visas, should verify any prospective employer against both federal lists before accepting an offer.

The US Department of Labor has updated its list of employers disqualified from participating in the H-1B visa program, effective July 1, 2026. The updated list now includes four companies barred from sponsoring H-1B workers due to willful violations of program rules — a critical reference for Indian professionals navigating the American work visa landscape.

Who's on the List

The four currently debarred employers are:

https://x.com/immigrationgirl/status/2080421857975566664
  • GowraTech, LLC — debarred from May 12, 2025 through May 11, 2027
  • Renotek Group LLC — debarred from August 8, 2025 through August 7, 2027
  • Seeloz, Inc. — debarred from March 4, 2026 through March 3, 2028
  • Sherwood at Mount Dora, Inc. (dba Sherwood Academy) — debarred from May 26, 2026 through May 25, 2028

All four were classified as willful violators of H-1B program rules by the Wage and Hour Division, meaning they deliberately violated conditions related to wages, working conditions, or other protections for H-1B workers.

The Willful Violator List

The Department also maintains a separate H-1B willful violator list, last updated June 29, 2026, which names 13 employers found to have committed serious violations. This broader list includes companies like Broadgate Inc., Virtulytix Inc., Macks USA Inc., Packet One LLC, SAAS IT Services LLC, Jericho Woodworks, BER-IT Inc., and Bonzer LLC, among others.

While the debarment list bars companies from sponsoring any new H-1B workers during their penalty period, the willful violator designation carries additional consequences. These employers face heightened scrutiny on any future labor condition applications and may be subject to additional compliance reviews by federal investigators.

What This Means for H-1B Workers

For the hundreds of thousands of Indian professionals who hold or seek H-1B visas — Indians received roughly 72% of all H-1B approvals in fiscal year 2025 — the debarment list serves as a critical due-diligence tool. Workers who accept positions with debarred employers risk visa complications, wage theft, and potential immigration status issues.

Immigration attorneys recommend that prospective H-1B workers check both the debarment list and the willful violator list before accepting any offer of employment. Both lists are publicly available on the Department of Labor's website.

"The Wage and Hour Division maintains these lists to protect workers and ensure employers who abuse the H-1B program face real consequences."

— US Department of Labor

Broader Context

The updated lists come amid a period of intense scrutiny of the H-1B program under the Trump administration. The White House has imposed a $100,000 surcharge on most new H-1B petitions, multiple major employers including Tata Consultancy Services and Cognizant have reduced or paused H-1B sponsorship, and the administration has signaled further restrictions are under consideration.

The Department of Labor also maintains a separate Permanent Labor Certification Program debarment list, which bars certain employers, attorneys, and agents from filing green card applications. That list was last updated in May 2025 and includes Hercules Staffing LLC and agent Dwight Molina.

Workers who suspect their employer is violating H-1B program rules can file complaints with the Wage and Hour Division. The complaints can be filed confidentially and are investigated regardless of the worker's immigration status.
